function: Deep Q-learning chooses the UAV movement and which IoT devices are scheduled on the L FDMA resources (above the physical layer); RIS phase shifts come from a non-learned DFT codebook search (p. 6; p. 7).
notes: above_phy: the learned component acts only on UAV trajectory and IoT device scheduling, both listed as above the physical layer. p. 6: "Sub-problem-1 addresses the UAV mobility and the scheduling of IoT devices, which are resolved through the application of deep Q-learning"; p. 7: "we built two different Q-networks for each action i.e. UAV trajectory and IoT devices scheduling decision". The only physical-layer decision, the RIS phase shifts, is not learned: p. 7: "a codebook is used to optimise the RISs phase shifts ... the received signal power is used to find the best configuration from the codebook". Transmit power is fixed (P = 20 dBm, Table I, p. 9), so no learned power or beam control; the work does not learn a physical-layer decision jointly with the above-PHY ones. Not no_learning (code 3), since the proposed method itself is DRL; code 4 is the one that describes it. For the reviewer to confirm: the paper calls the scheduling "radio resource allocation" (p. 3: "leveraging DRL for UAV trajectory and resource allocation optimisation"; p. 6), but the learned variable is the binary scheduling decision eta_i[n] (p. 5, (12), with at most L = 3 devices per slot, (14e)) and the action is "IoT devices wireless scheduling, where the agent selects a subset L from the total IoT devices I" (p. 6). If that selection were read as learned resource allocation in an aerial link, the work would pass Step 1 as area 6. Title and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3608968 match on p. 1 of the PDF.
